title: Penne con Melanzane
subtitle: Pasta with roasted aubergine and tomato sauce
excerpt: Penne tossed in a rich tomato sauce with roasted aubergine. Roasting the aubergine separately before adding it to the sauce avoids the greasy, soggy result of frying, and gives pieces with crisp edges and a creamy interior.

recipe.sourceNotes: Aubergine pasta is widespread across southern Italy and Sicily, where aubergines are in season through the summer and autumn. The most famous version is pasta alla Norma, a Sicilian dish with fried aubergine, tomato, fresh basil, and ricotta salata, named after the Bellini opera. This version roasts the aubergine and omits the cheese for a simpler, lighter dish that works year-round using tinned tomatoes.

content.text: Roasting the aubergine at high heat in a generous amount of olive oil gives you pieces with golden, caramelised edges rather than the pale, soggy result of gentle roasting or the oil-saturated result of frying. Cut the pieces no smaller than 3 cm so they hold their shape. The tomato sauce is simple: garlic, chilli, tinned tomatoes, and time.

Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Toss the aubergine chunks with 60 ml of the olive oil and a good pinch of salt. Spread on a large roasting tin in a single layer. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and caramelised, turning once halfway.

In a frying pan over medium heat, warm the remaining olive oil. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, season, and simmer for 15 minutes, breaking up the tomatoes.
Cook the penne in heavily salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 100 ml pasta water and drain.
Fold the roasted aubergine into the tomato sauce. Toss with the drained penne, adding pasta water to loosen if needed. Scatter with fresh basil and serve.
